comparison: Perfect alignment on β-cell loss and cellular composition findings (C18-C21). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers treating them as confirmatory evidence validating the CODEX methodology.

Perfect alignment on T cell population differences between Inflamed and Insulin-Depleted islets (C57-C60). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as part of the advanced characterization of insulitis stages.

Strong alignment on study design and methodology (C10-C17). OpenEval includes C12 (cohort selection rationale) which peer review does not explicitly address, but both find the CODEX methodology and cohort composition well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as a major strength.

Strong alignment on IDO expression findings (C28-C36, C91-C93). Both evaluations find this novel observation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers identify it as a 'notable finding' with potential therapeutic implications, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of appropriate speculation.

Strong alignment on pseudotime reconstruction and three-stage classification (C23-C27, C90). Both find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly note consistency with prior work (Damond et al.) and treat this as confirmatory validation, matching OpenEval's assessment.

Strong alignment on lobular patterning analysis (C63-C71, C106-C107, C109). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the novel insight about crosstalk between islet and extra-islet compartments, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of appropriate speculation.

Strong alignment on cohort size limitations (C117-C121). Both evaluations find the authors' acknowledgment of this limitation SUPPORTED. All peer reviewers explicitly recognize this limitation but accept it given the rarity of suitable samples, matching OpenEval's assessment.

Moderate alignment on TLS spatial relationships (C84-C89, C81-C83, C113). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the spatial analysis and potential role of TLSs as T cell entry points, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of reasonable but speculative inferences.
